clue.text: Man confronts priest, one leaving place of worship

indicators.note: the man stands face to face with, so in front of, the priest that follows

parts.note: a chap is a man, an everyday word for a fellow

indicators.note: the word one names a letter that walks out of the priest's name

parts.note: Eli is the Old Testament priest who brought up Samuel
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A man faces down a clergyman while somebody walks out of the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' drops the I from Eli. 'Confronts' sounds hostile but only places the man first.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapel is a small church or a room set aside for prayer, so a building for religious services.

clue.text: Dramatic fellow's musical piece gets cut short

parts.note: fellow's means belonging to him, which is his
a trio is a piece of music written for three players

indicators.note: the verb for gets loses its final letter, as if trimmed at the end

parts.note: to nick is to get hold of something, as in steal or catch

explanation.surface: A man's chamber composition is being abbreviated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' takes the K off NICK, leaving NIC. NICK is British slang for steal or get.
explanation.definitionFit: Histrionic behaviour is theatrical and over-emotional, like acting on a stage.

clue.text: Complaint by top player at important match

parts.note: a pro is a professional, a player at the top level
a Test is an important international match, especially in cricket

explanation.surface: A star player grumbles at a big game.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is the top-level international game in cricket and rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: A protest is an objection or expression of disapproval.

clue.text: Floral decoration of little interest (very little)

indicators.note: of here means made from part of the words that follow, which hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: Somebody dismisses a flower garland as barely worth a glance.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across littLE Interest; the bracketed 'very little' remarks that the answer is a tiny word.
explanation.definitionFit: A lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers worn round the neck.

clue.text: After work's over, to relax in a gym is just right

indicators.note: the work and the rest are placed inside the word for gym

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school gym class

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for work is read from its end

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work, and the 's is a link
to sit is to rest or relax in a chair

explanation.surface: After a shift ends, chilling out at the gym is the perfect move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the work round to read backwards; 'in' puts it and the rest inside school gym, after A. 'After' is only scene-setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Apposite means apt or well suited to the situation.

clue.text: A firm refusal to lead single African kingdom

indicators.note: the earlier pieces go in front of the word for single

parts.note: shan't, shall not, is a flat refusal
single means one, the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A flat no is going to head a lone African realm.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ashanti were a powerful West African state in what is now Ghana.

clue.text: Concert one attends unaccompanied, with happy outcome expected?

parts.note: a prom is a concert, as in the London Proms
one is the Roman numeral I
singly means alone, one at a time

explanation.surface: Going to a concert on your own looks like it could end well.
explanation.walkthrough: The Proms are a famous summer series of concerts in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Promisingly describes something going in a hopeful way, with signs of success.

clue.text: Weapon recently stolen by thug finally wrapped in newspaper

indicators.note: the stolen goods and the letter go inside the paper, like fish and chips

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
hot goods have been freshly stolen

indicators.note: finally takes only the closing letter of thug

explanation.surface: A thug's freshly nicked gun is hidden in a rolled-up paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper; 'wrapped in' places the stolen goods and the thug's last letter inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A shotgun is a long gun firing a spray of pellets.

clue.text: Rook caught in trap set up for seabird

indicators.note: the rook is trapped inside the other piece
in a down clue set up means written upwards, so the word for trap reads backwards

parts.note: a net is a trap
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A rook is snared in a trap that was laid for a sea bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns NET into TEN, and R goes inside it. Rook looks like the bird, but it is the chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A tern is a slender gull-like bird of coasts.

clue.text: Wood — a great amount is stored for floor

indicators.note: the great amount and is are kept inside the wood

parts.note: ash is a tree and its timber
a ton is informal for a lot
taken as written

explanation.surface: A large quantity of timber is kept for laying a floor.
explanation.walkthrough: Floor is a verb here: to stun or bowl over.
explanation.definitionFit: To floor someone is to amaze them so much they are knocked flat.

clue.text: Smells of a flower, you say?

indicators.note: you say signals that the word is to be heard rather than spelled

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river; of the Oder is Oder's

explanation.surface: Someone asks if the scents come from a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is read as flow-er, a river: here the Oder, on the German-Polish border. ODER'S said out loud matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Odours are scents, often unpleasant ones.

clue.text: Independent and Liberal seeking election

parts.note: liberal can mean free, as in a free hand
a candidate standing is running for election

explanation.surface: A politician runs in an election as an independent Liberal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Independent' and 'Liberal' look like party labels.
explanation.definitionFit: Something freestanding is self-supporting, not attached to anything else.

clue.text: Faulty tone — help is given after very little time … by me?

definitions.text: Faulty tone — help is given after very little time … by me?

indicators.note: the shuffled letters come after the time letter

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time, the smallest form of the word

indicators.note: faulty means broken, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A caller with a bad line gets help after a brief moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Faulty' rearranges the three words, and 'given after' puts the result behind the time letter. The whole clue is spoken by the operator who helps on a bad line.
explanation.definitionFit: A switchboard operator answers calls and puts callers through.

clue.text: Plump bird's petition?

parts.note: round means plump, chubby
a robin is a bird, and the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A fat bird puts in a request.
explanation.walkthrough: Signatures on a round robin were written in a circle so no name headed the list.
explanation.definitionFit: A round robin is a petition signed by many people.

clue.text: Italian course could be a piece of cake to learners in Italy

parts.note: a torte is a rich cake
L is learner, as on British learner drivers' plates; two make learners
taken as written
I is the international car code for Italy

explanation.surface: An Italian class might be easy for students who are in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece of cake' looks like easy, but it is a cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Tortellini, stuffed pasta rings, may be served as a pasta course.

clue.text: Retreat not sanctioned?

parts.note: no means not
OK means approved or sanctioned

explanation.surface: A withdrawal that has not been authorised.
explanation.definitionFit: A nook is a secluded corner to withdraw into.

clue.text: Bacon portion consumed by customer in diner

indicators.note: the letters are eaten up within the words customer in diner

explanation.surface: A diner customer eats the bacon.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across customeR IN Diner.
explanation.definitionFit: Rind is the tough outer skin cut from bacon.

clue.text: Refuse a month's work

parts.note: Dec is short for December; the 's is a link
a line is a line of work, an occupation

explanation.surface: Someone turns down a month's labour.
explanation.definitionFit: To decline is to say no to an offer.

clue.text: Near entrance to park, high-spirited young lad runs inside … this?

definitions.text: Near entrance to park, high-spirited young lad runs inside … this?

indicators.note: near says this letter sits right beside the rest
entrance to means the opening letter of park
inside puts the runs letter within the shuffled words
high-spirited means wild and lively, so the letters jump about

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A lively boy runs about near the gates of a park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high-spirited' rearranges the two words to LAYGOUND; 'inside' puts R within it, and 'Near' sets P from park at the front. The whole clue pictures where the lad runs.
explanation.definitionFit: A play area is a place for children to run about outdoors.

clue.text: Medusas swim about freely, it's supposed

indicators.note: swimming about freely mixes the letters of the word Medusas

explanation.surface: Jellyfish drift about at will, so people think.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medusas' is the plural of medusa, a jellyfish.
explanation.definitionFit: Assumed means taken for granted, presumed true.

clue.text: Dance round home to record

parts.note: O is round in shape
a nest is a bird's home
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A dancer circles back home to make a recording.
explanation.definitionFit: The one-step is an early twentieth-century ballroom dance.

clue.text: It's true about Lawrence leading the army out

indicators.note: leading puts the name in front of the scrambled army

parts.note: c, circa, means about
T. E. Lawrence enlisted in the RAF under the name Ross

indicators.note: out means disordered, so the letters of the army are shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone swears that Lawrence led the troops out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges THE ARMY into MYHEART. Lawrence of Arabia used the alias Ross.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross my heart is a solemn promise that what you say is honest.

clue.text: Stacked up boxes of documents left by Independent writer

indicators.note: in a down clue stacked up means the letters run upwards, so they read backwards
the letter for Independent departs from the word

parts.note: files are boxes or folders holding documents

explanation.surface: Box files are piled high by a writer for the Independent newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: FILES less I is FLES; 'Stacked up' turns it upward. Writer here means the person writing, me.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer speaking of themselves says 'myself', so the writer is one's own person.

clue.text: Sign, say, knocked over by small car

indicators.note: the two letters are toppled and run backwards

parts.note: eg, for example, means say
the Mini is a small British car

explanation.surface: A road sign is knocked down by a little car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' turns EG into GE.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemini, the Twins, is a zodiac sign.

clue.text: Province's aim: to ban carousing

indicators.note: carousing is drunken revelry, so the letters run riot

explanation.surface: A Canadian province plans to outlaw drunken parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Manitoba is one of the Canadian provinces.

clue.text: Appear drowsy, and teacher will get upset

indicators.note: in a down clue get upset means turned upside down, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: A student looks sleepy and the lecturer is annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: To nod is to let the head drop when falling asleep.

clue.text: Deeply moved? That's not genuine

explanation.definitionFit: Affected means emotionally touched, and also artificial or pretentious in manner.

clue.text: Supplying drug to despicable type grabbing fix

indicators.note: the cad seizes the other word and holds it inside

parts.note: a dog is a contemptible person
to pin is to fix in place

explanation.surface: A drug pusher, a lowlife, grabs a fix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fix' suggests a drug dose, but it means pin.
explanation.definitionFit: Doping is giving someone drugs, as with athletes or horses.
